proof:
# Mixed depth is at most the number of positive fibers times own depth

This is an upper bound, not an OC lower bound. It also strengthens the
interpretation of the proper critical BM-equality three-fiber theorem.

## Statement and conventions

Let n>=0 and d>=1. Let C be a bounded convex set in R^n times R^d
whose nonempty integer fibers are compact, and suppose at least one
fiber has positive d-volume. Let P be the finite set of integer bases
whose fibers C_z have positive d-volume, and let N=|P|. Zero-volume
fibers may be present and have zero mass throughout this statement.
Use the measure

    mu(E)=sum_z |E_z|_d.

Fix z_0 in P and y in K=C_(z_0). Define the ordinary raw depth

    f_K(y)=inf_{u!=0}|K intersect {x:u.x>=u.y}|,

and the mixed raw depth

    D_S(z_0,y)=inf{mu(S intersect H):H closed ambient halfspace,
                                      (z_0,y) in H},

where S=C intersect (Z^n times R^d). Then

    D_S(z_0,y)<=N f_K(y).                            (1)

The proof is finite and uses only convex combinations of actual
integer fibers. It requires no regularity or affine extension of
the integer-sampled quantile function.

## 1. Finite affine-majorant lemma

For finitely many v_j in R^n and w_j in R, there exists b in R^n with

    b.v_j>=w_j for every j                           (2)

if and only if every finite family lambda_j>=0 satisfying
sum lambda_j v_j=0 also satisfies sum lambda_j w_j<=0.

Necessity follows by summing (2). Here is a self-contained sufficiency
argument. Consider the cone G generated by (v_j,w_j) and (0,-1) in
R^(n+1). It is closed. Indeed any conic combination can have its
support reduced to linearly independent generators: in a dependent
support, choose a nonzero linear dependence, reverse its sign if
necessary so one coefficient is positive, and subtract the largest
nonnegative multiple that preserves all conic coefficients. At least
one coefficient becomes zero. Repeat. The cone is consequently a
finite union of cones generated by linearly independent subsets.
Each such cone is closed, since its linear parametrization is a
homeomorphism onto a closed linear subspace and maps the closed
orthant to that cone.

Under the stated condition e=(0,1) is not in G: a representation
would give sum lambda_j v_j=0 and sum lambda_j w_j>=1. Choose a
nearest point p of the closed cone G to e, which exists by restricting
the minimization to a sufficiently large compact ball. Put a=e-p.
The usual squared-distance comparison along segments in G gives
a.(g-p)<=0 for all g in G. Choosing g=0 and g=2p gives a.p=0, so
a.g<=0 for all g in G and a.e=|a|^2>0. In particular the final
coordinate a_(n+1)>0. Thus b=-a_(1:n)/a_(n+1) satisfies (2).

## 2. Equal-volume cap quantiles provide the required inequalities

Fix a nonzero continuous normal u and a proper level s in the middle
fiber K, and put

    q=|K intersect {u.x>=s}|,  0<q<|K|.

Only constrain bases z for which |C_z|>q. Each such fiber is a
d-dimensional convex body. Its tail volume is continuous and strictly
decreasing between its two support levels, so there is a unique
proper quantile h_z satisfying

    |C_z intersect {u.x>=h_z}|=q.                    (3)

Continuity follows by dominated convergence since a proper or
supporting hyperplane has zero d-volume. Strict decrease between
support levels follows because every nonempty open slab between
those levels intersects the body's interior in positive volume.
In particular z_0 is constrained and h_(z_0)=s.

Let lambda_z>=0 sum to one over constrained bases and satisfy
sum lambda_z z=z_0. Convexity of the actual set C gives

    sum_z lambda_z [C_z intersect {u.x>=h_z}]
      subset K intersect {u.x>=sum_z lambda_z h_z}.

Brunn--Minkowski, iterated over this finite family, bounds the volume
root of the left side below by sum lambda_z q^(1/d)=q^(1/d).
The middle tail at sum lambda_z h_z therefore has volume at least q.
Since s is its proper q-quantile, strict decrease implies

    sum_z lambda_z h_z<=s.                           (4)

Apply the preceding finite lemma to v_z=z-z_0 and w_z=h_z-s.
Every nonzero nonnegative dependence can be normalized to weights
summing to one, and (4) gives exactly its required sign. Hence a
finite vector b exists with

    h_z<=s+b.(z-z_0)

for every constrained base.

The actual ambient halfspace

    H={ (z,x):u.x>=s+b.(z-z_0) }                     (5)

therefore captures at most q in every constrained fiber. Every
unconstrained fiber has whole volume at most q, regardless of its
threshold. Zero-volume fibers contribute nothing. Thus

    mu(S intersect H)<=Nq.                           (6)

The continuous part of the ambient normal is u!=0, so (5) is always
a legitimate halfspace, even if b=0 or n=0.

## 3. Positive and zero ordinary depths

The map u -> |K intersect {u.x>=u.y}| is continuous on the unit
sphere, again because each boundary hyperplane has zero d-volume.
Thus f_K(y) is attained. Opposite through-y cap volumes add to |K|,
so f_K(y)<=|K|/2.

If f_K(y)>0, choose a minimizing u. Its source level s=u.y is
proper, with q=f_K(y)<|K|. The halfspace in (5) contains (z_0,y)
on its boundary, and (6) proves (1).

If f_K(y)=0, choose an attaining normal u. Since y belongs to K,
s=u.y equals its maximum support level in this direction. For
epsilon>0 sufficiently small, the level s-epsilon is proper and
the corresponding cap volume q_epsilon is positive and tends to
zero. Applying (5)--(6) at that level produces a halfspace containing
(z_0,y) strictly, of mass at most Nq_epsilon. Taking the infimum over
these legitimate containing halfspaces gives D_S(z_0,y)=0.
No limiting halfspace, bounded normal sequence, or attaining zero-mass
cap is required. This completes (1), including source boundary points.

## 4. Consequence for the proper critical three-fiber BM cover

Under the hypotheses of
`candidate 9f6a0ee7f33d8c84`,
the three-fiber calculation gives Q=3q, where every middle trace
has volume q. Applying (1), with N=3, at the actual source yields

    3q=Q<=3 f_K(y),

while one displayed middle trace gives f_K(y)<=q. Hence f_K(y)=q.
For any other point x in K, the middle trace cover supplies a trace
containing x of volume q, so f_K(x)<=q. Consequently

    q=max_{x in K} f_K(x),
    y is an ordinary deepest point of K.            (7)

Uniqueness is not needed or asserted here. The source need not be
the ordinary centroid, and q/|K| need not equal Gamma_d. The exact
truncated-triangle critical nongluing example has q/|K|>Gamma_2,
so (7) is consistent with its nonhomothetic endpoint bodies.

## Scope

Only d-volume and a positive d-dimensional source fiber are treated.
This note does not identify changing intrinsic Hausdorff direction
spaces when all integer fibers have lower dimension. The constructed
normal can have an arbitrarily large integer-coordinate part; no
bounded-slope assertion is made. All halfspaces are closed, and
zero-volume boundary sections cause no omitted mass in this measure.
The factor N depends on the number of positive fibers and provides
no lower bound of the OC form.
